root_cause.text: In the SCMI firmware notifier path (`drivers/firmware/arm_scmi/notify.c`), `__scmi_event_handler_get_ops()` could return `NULL` on handler lookup/creation failure even though its callers expected an `ERR_PTR`, causing a NULL dereference on the notify error path when that return value was treated as an error pointer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the documented return contract from “NULL on Failure” to “ERR_PTR on Failure” and fixes the function to `return hndl ?: ERR_PTR(-ENODEV);`, while the CVE description says call chains “expect an ERR_PTR to be returned on failure” but the helper “can still return a NULL when no handler could be found or created.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In the SCMI firmware notifier path (`drivers/firmware/arm_scmi/notify.c`), `__scmi_event_handler_get_ops()` could return `NULL` on handler lookup/creation failure even though its callers expected an `ERR_PTR`, causing a NULL dereference on the notify error path when that return value was treated as an error pointer.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes the documented return contract from “NULL on Failure” to “ERR_PTR on Failure” and fixes the function to `return hndl ?: ERR_PTR(-ENODEV);`, while the CVE description says call chains “expect an ERR_PTR to be returned on failure” but the helper “can still return a NULL when no handler could be found or created.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the documentation for __scmi_event_handler_get_ops() to describe ERR_PTR-based failure returns instead of NULL.
intent_record.what: The kernel-doc comment for __scmi_event_handler_get_ops() was updated: the documented failure return value changed from "NULL" to "ERR_PTR" while the function signature and code shown remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior in the shown hunk; it corrects the documented API contract to indicate that failure is represented by an error-encoded pointer rather than a NULL pointer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return an explicit -ENODEV error pointer when no SCMI event handler is available.
intent_record.what: The function return statement was changed from `return hndl;` to `return hndl ?: ERR_PTR(-ENODEV);`, adding a fallback that converts a NULL `hndl` into an `ERR_PTR(-ENODEV)` error value.
intent_record.how: At runtime, callers no longer receive a raw NULL pointer when no event handler is found; instead, they get a standardized error pointer indicating the device is unavailable, which makes failure handling more explicit and prevents ambiguous NULL returns.

grouping_result.intent: Return an explicit -ENODEV error pointer when no SCMI event handler is available.

consistency_review.core_intent: Make SCMI event handler lookup and documentation consistently use ERR_PTR-style failure returns, including -ENODEV when no handler is available.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: they fix __scmi_event_handler_get_ops() to use ERR_PTR-style failures instead of returning NULL, including -ENODEV when no handler is available, which prevents the NULL dereference on the notify error path.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body does not contain the root-cause construct. In this commit, `__scmi_event_handler_get_ops()` explicitly returns a pointer or `NULL` on failure: the comment says `"Return: A properly refcounted handler on Success, NULL on Failure"`, and the code does `if (!hndl && create) { ... if (hndl && scmi_register_event_handler(...)) { ... hndl = NULL; } } return hndl;`. There is no `ERR_PTR`/`IS_ERR` style error-pointer handling here, so the specific NULL-dereference bug described for later callers treating the return as an error pointer is not present in this version. The function also does not contain the later fix of returning an error pointer instead of NULL, so `is_fixed` is also false.
